findings.title: Markov health-test threshold violations can never generate a failure
findings.location: Final output assignments for test_fail_hi_pulse_o and test_fail_lo_pulse_o near end of module
findings.description: The Markov health-test module receives programmable high and low thresholds, tracks per-stream transition-pair counters, computes the selected maximum/minimum/sum counter values, and exposes itself as an entropy health test. Nevertheless, both failure outputs are unconditionally tied to 1'b0. Consequently, an RNG stream whose transition statistics violate markov_hi_thresholds or markov_lo_thresholds cannot be rejected or counted as a health-test failure through this module. The generated register interface exposes Markov threshold registers, and entropy_src documentation lists the Markov test as protection against correlated noise, so the synthesized tie-offs defeat an advertised entropy-quality check rather than merely suppressing simulation diagnostics. An attacker capable of influencing the physical noise source toward a correlated pattern may therefore reduce seed entropy without triggering the configured Markov failure path; other health tests may detect some patterns but do not restore the missing transition-correlation invariant.
findings.recommendation: Implement synthesized high- and low-threshold comparisons at the completed health-test window, analogous to entropy_src_adaptp_ht: assert test_fail_hi_pulse_o when active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && test_cnt_hi_o > thresh_hi_i, and assert test_fail_lo_pulse_o when active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && test_cnt_lo_o < thresh_lo_i. Verify that both pulses are included in the core's any-failure aggregation, alert counters, startup acceptance decision, continuous-test rejection path, and recoverable-alert handling. If the Markov test is intentionally unsupported, remove or lock its configuration/status interface and documentation and ensure the unsupported test cannot be represented as active or relied upon for entropy qualification.
